title: Ddev Plastiks Industries Ltd - 543547 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 13% and PAT reached INR202 crore (+9%); FY27 guidance is 2.31 lakh tonnes volume at 73% utilisation, with BESS excluded.
summary.overview: Ddev Plastiks reported FY26 revenue up 13% YoY, EBITDA up 12% at an 11% margin, and PAT of INR202 crore (+9%). Volumes were 2,01,370 tonnes at 77% capacity utilisation, with exports up 30% and export volumes up 23%. Management said the Israel-Iran conflict from 28 February 2026 raised raw material costs by 50%-plus and briefly hurt demand, but supply and pricing have stabilised since April. The company guided FY27 volume to 2.31 lakh tonnes, 13% revenue growth and ~11% EBITDA margin, and announced a foray into battery energy storage systems (BESS) targeting 5 GWh.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR10 crore MTM gain on debtors; ~INR11 crore forward-contract loss in other expenses; net ~INR1 crore

segments.name: Polymer compounding (cables and wires)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 2,01,370 tonnes at 77% utilisation; the company says the 30,000 tpa of new PVC and HFFR capacity had limited operating time in the year. Installed capacity is 2,68,400 tpa, rising beyond 315,000 tpa with the Bhiwadi XLPE addition of 48,000 tpa (commercial operations from last week of April 2026).

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: New vertical; FY27 revenue expected at INR200-250 crore, with breakeven at roughly INR200-plus crore. FY28 target is 1 GWh and INR800-900 crore revenue at 10%-plus EBITDA margin (INR80-90 crore). Long-term aim is 5 GWh, or INR2,000-2,500 crore. Excluded from FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target 2,31,000 tpa at 73% capacity utilisation, with 13% revenue growth; BESS revenue excluded and additional.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 11%.
FY28 polymer volume growth guided at ~15% over FY27 base (about 2.3 lakh to ~2.65 lakh tonnes).
FY27 capex plan of ~INR175 crore, of which ~INR70 crore is for BESS and the rest mainly XLPE compound capacity.
Long-term target: INR5,000 crore consolidated polymer compounding revenue by FY30, plus BESS revenue.
Q1 FY27 export growth expected to continue; management declined to guide export growth beyond Q1 given geopolitical uncertainty.
XLPE compound for 220 kV targeted by 2030; 440 kV to follow later.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 2,68,400 tpa, with a further 48,000 tpa XLPE at Bhiwadi commissioned from late April 2026 (committed capex ~INR80 crore); total capacity above 315,000 tpa.
Management said 80,000 tonnes of the 315,000 tpa total came online in the last four months; the 48,000 tpa Bhiwadi unit is expected to be fully utilised in FY27-FY28.
FY27 capex ~INR175 crore, of which ~INR70 crore for BESS in the first phase.
BESS: 5 GW phased target, with each GW generating about INR800-900 crore revenue; the first phase needs ~INR200-250 crore of working capital, funded from existing limits and internal cash.

BESS sourcing: lithium cells, enclosures, harness, DC cables, sensors and liquid cooling are sourced from identified suppliers; BMS is to be imported from China initially, with in-house BMS and EMS planned.
demand_pricing: Management said price pass-through is typically 7-15 days, becoming instant during sharp spikes such as March 2026; EBITDA is held at a fixed INR14-15 per kg.

Raw material prices rose 50%-plus during the conflict and have since stabilised. About 10-15% of raw material is imported, mainly from the Middle East and Europe; supply normalised by mid-April per management.
Export growth came from MENA and Europe; Latin America and North America showed no growth. Consignments stuck in March due to logistics moved in April.
Competition in XLPE is from Dow and Borealis; in HFFR from Shakun Polymer (now Orbia); in low-voltage fire-retardant from KLJ Polymers. Management said China import pressure is manageable.
Customers are mostly on contracts of up to ~90 days, with back-to-back import bookings; no open-ended annual contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 guidance imply NSR degrowth, given 13% revenue growth and 15% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is built on FY26 average realisation as a conservative base; Q1 NSR is expected to be much higher given the escalations.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BESS excluded from guidance and what is the breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: First-year ramp-up is the reason; breakeven is at roughly INR200-plus crore of revenue, and no FY27 loss is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government spending slowdown a risk to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to private solar (Adani, Tata, JSW, Reliance), grid and peak-demand needs, and Middle East reconstruction demand, and said there is no expected impact on demand or cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 and BESS margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Total FY27 outlay is INR175 crore including BESS, of which ~INR70 crore goes to BESS; BESS margins are 5-8% lower than compounding in FY27, rising above 10% in the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS approval cycle and supplier base?
qa_highlights.answer: Developer approvals take 3-6 months, with certifications (ISO/IEC standards) in progress; suppliers are identified and locked for a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Where does BESS IP sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial BMS will be imported from China; the company plans its own BMS and EMS IP in the coming months.

risks_watch: Geopolitical volatility (Israel-Iran conflict) on raw material costs, supply and export logistics; management gave no export growth guidance beyond Q1.
FY27 volume of 2.31 lakh tonnes is well below the 3.15 lakh tonne installed capacity, so utilisation depends on the ramp of new capacity; the 73% target is conservative.
BESS execution: certifications, factory readiness, dependence on Chinese BMS imports, and the working capital needed (INR200-250 crore) for the first GWh.
Backward integration by cable customers, and China import pressure in the compounds segment.
Other income in Q4 was mainly MTM gains; the net impact was only ~INR1 crore after forward-contract losses, so earnings quality should be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core polymer business and on FY27 targets, but cautious on export visibility beyond Q1 and on raw material volatility. Management was evasive on export growth percentages and on exact BESS revenue timing, and gave conservative guidance on purpose.
key_quotes: Our HFR capacity sustained utilization of nearly 50% throughout this period of turbulence.
So, we do not see any impact on our demand or our financials or our cash flows because of this perceived cut in the government spending.
So, we are targeting breakeven in this particular financial year, achieving a turnover of close to INR250-odd crores.
So, we don't want to have, you can say, aggressive estimates, which may be difficult to comment tomorrow.

adds.what: 48,000 tpa XLPE compound capacity at Bhiwadi (commercial operations from last week of April 2026)
30,000 tpa PVC and HFFR capacity (added in FY26, limited operating time in year)
BESS vertical: 1 GWh FY28 target, 5 GWh long-term aim (MWh/GWh capacity, not a plant-level count)

growth.why: FY27 guided to 231,000 t volume at 73% utilisation and 13% revenue growth with ~11% EBITDA margin, backed by the 48,000 tpa Bhiwadi XLPE unit (live from late April 2026) and 80,000 t of capacity added in the last four months, though no quarterly Q4 revenue or EBITDA growth figures were stated and BESS revenue of INR200-250 crore is excluded from guidance.
